summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR316 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 21%; FY27 guidance now exceeded.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 30% YoY and 53% QoQ to INR316 crore, driven by volumes (about 10-15% in kg terms) and better price realisation. Gross margin was 35% and EBITDA rose 40% to INR68 crore at a 21% margin, with PAT up 57% to INR39.6 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 19% to INR523 crore and PAT grew 36% to INR59.8 crore. Management now expects to exceed both the 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs 32% a year ago; 36% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: INR59.8 crore; INR60.8 crore incl. share of VKT profit

financial_highlights.change: +25% YoY, on ibuprofen demand from regulated markets

financial_highlights.metric: High-value API share of revenue (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: management says ~150 days reasonable; previously 180-220 days

segments.name: ARV
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue grew 47% to INR150 crore, attributed to market share gains.

segments.name: Anti-inflammatory (ibuprofen)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue grew 25% to INR110 crore; utilisation at 90-95%, running ~400-500 tonnes per month. EBITDA margin in the teens per management; pre-backward integration margin was below 10%.

segments.name: Other therapeutic areas
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 growth: anti-migraine 32%, anti-epileptic 44%, anti-anginal 45%, anti-ED 52%.

segments.name: Peptides (SMS Peptides Pvt Ltd, 99.9% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Peptides R&D facility fully operational; INR50 crore loan approved for subsidiary. Pilot-scale production targeted Q4 FY27; first CRO revenue expected Q2 FY28. Management cites 40%+ margins for peptides, though too early to quantify for its own products.

segments.name: CDMO (SMS coLab Pvt Ltd, wholly owned)
segments.commentary: Set up as a dedicated CDMO platform for APIs and peptides; no facility yet, so no customer discussions as of the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance raised: management now expects to exceed prior guidance of 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA margin, given strong H1 and pricing in key APIs expected to stay stable near term.
FY28 EBITDA margin target of 22-24%, per management in Q&A.
6-8 new molecules expected to start commercial production in FY28; these scale over the following six quarters and are expected to be EBITDA accretive.
Raw material and pricing pressure expected to continue for 1-2 quarters, per management.
Ibuprofen capacity to reach 9,600 tonnes per year; ibuprofen share of revenue to remain below 30-35% of revenue, with no single product above 35% dependence.
DMF/CEP filings target of 10 for FY27; 6 completed so far (4 in H1, 2 in October).
capex_capacity: Capex programme of INR280 crore: INR160 crore deployed so far; remaining INR120 crore to be deployed before FY27 end; on track for completion in FY27.

Ibuprofen capacity to rise to 9,600 tonnes per year from the current ~400-500 tonnes per month; remaining ibuprofen capex to take 1-2 quarters; full ~90% occupancy of 9,600 tonnes expected in 6-9 months after that.
Ibuprofen utilisation at 90-95% on existing capacity; batch sizes close to 10 tonnes.
Capex adds capacity for existing molecules and for 6-8 new molecules in the pipeline.
Peptides: ~30 chemists, mostly PhDs; recruitment ongoing; dedicated peptides CEO in place.
demand_pricing: Volume growth in Q2 about 10-15% YoY in kg terms; balance of the 30% revenue growth from price realisation.
Ibuprofen prices cited at $8-9 per kg currently, versus $7 or below some time back; management says prices are cyclical.

Management sees possible ibuprofen price improvement as peers shut capacity and SMS moves towards US and European markets; also developing ibuprofen derivatives and salts, which carry higher margins but lower volumes.
Management says high-value products are growing as a share of revenue; new products are mostly non-commodity.
Customer interest reported from US customers after trade shows; no peptide samples sent to customers yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt level expected by year end, given capex and working capital needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said combined long-term and short-term debt would be around INR400 crore by year end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth and price hike contribution in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was about 10-15% in kg terms. Raw material prices were also raised, with pressure expected for 1-2 more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is targeted for next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management indicated 22-24% EBITDA margin, helped by product mix and easing raw material pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the peptide pilot a CRO opportunity or in-house product?
qa_highlights.answer: It is SMS's own generic peptide development, not a CRO contract; pilot scale by Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle to assume going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 120-150 days, with ~150 days a reasonable planning figure given domestic ibuprofen credit terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is fixed asset turnover excluding CWIP?
qa_highlights.answer: 1.72x currently, against 1.46x including CWIP; management expects improvement, with a 1.75x target.

risks_watch: Debt rising to about INR400 crore by year end to fund capex and working capital; watch net debt and interest cost.
Ibuprofen is cyclical; prices moved from below $7 to $8-9 per kg, and the business is still ramping capacity.
Peptides and CDMO are pre-revenue; first CRO revenue expected Q2 FY28 and CDMO facility not yet set up.
Ramp-up timing of 6-8 new molecules in FY28 and the six-quarter scale-up period.
Raw material cost pressure expected for 1-2 more quarters; gross margin fell QoQ from 36% to 35%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on H1 numbers and on raising guidance. Management was less specific or evasive on ibuprofen margins and peptide economics, citing confidentiality or being too early. Some answers were disjointed due to audio issues.
key_quotes: Backward integration gives us a structural cost advantage, not a temporary pricing benefit.
So both put together will be around INR400 crores by end of this year.

growth.why: Management now expects to exceed FY27 guidance of 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA margin, backed by H1 revenue up 19% and utilisation at 90-95%, with ibuprofen capacity rising to 9,600 t/yr in 1-2 quarters after the remaining capex and 6-10 new molecules due in FY28, though specific order or contract numbers were not given.

mgmt.note: A dedicated peptides CEO is in place for SMS Peptides; no change date or growth plan details were given beyond the peptides pilot targeted for Q4 FY27.
initiatives: Peptides pilot-scale production targeted Q4 FY27
First CRO revenue expected Q2 FY28

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided FY28 EBITDA margin 22-24% (vs 21% in Q2 FY27 and H1 FY27) on mix and easing raw material pressure, though raw material pressure persists for 1-2 quarters and Q2 gross margin slipped to 35% from 36%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ibuprofen capacity rises to 9,600 t/yr after remaining ~INR120 crore capex (1-2 quarters), with ~90% occupancy 6-9 months later; utilisation is 90-95% today on existing capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew ~10-15% in kg terms, ARV revenue +47% and anti-inflammatory +25% in H1, and new capacity plus 6-8 molecules in FY28 support further throughput.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 90-95% with the INR280 crore programme (INR160 crore deployed) still under way; no new programme announced, but the 22-24% margin and 6-8 molecule pipeline point to further expansion beyond current plans.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management now expects to exceed 15% FY27 revenue growth and 20% EBITDA margin, backed by H1 revenue +19% and PAT +36%, with Q2 EBITDA margin at 21%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance was raised, but raw material and pricing pressure for 1-2 quarters and ibuprofen cyclicality (price $8-9/kg vs below $7 earlier) are the main risks to watch.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management expects 6-8 new molecules to start commercial production in FY28, scaling over six quarters and EBITDA accretive; peptides pilot-scale production targeted Q4 FY27 with first CRO revenue in Q2 FY28.

rows.label: Debt rising to about INR400 crore by year end
rows.why: Combined debt is guided to ~INR400 crore by year end to fund capex and working capital, so leverage rises before it falls, which is a net negative in the window.

rows.label: Working capital cycle guided to 120-150 days
rows.why: Cycle has fallen from 180-220 days to a planning figure of about 150 days, and cash conversion is ~93-95% in H1 FY27 against ~72% long-term.

rows.label: US and European ibuprofen and peptide customer interest
rows.why: Management is moving towards US and European markets with customer interest after trade shows, but no peptide samples have gone out yet and no contracts were quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 numbers, the guidance raise and the 22-24% FY28 margin target, but evasive on ibuprofen margins and peptide economics; analysts pushed on volume versus price contribution, raw material pressure and debt, and audio issues disrupted some answers.
